1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 08.05.2023.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 08.05.2023 at about 5-40 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Yeshwanthapura Traffic Police Station, in front of Shakthi Health Meats Pvt. Ltd., near Surana college, ESI Hospital road, when the Petitioner was riding the M.V.C.No.4086/2023 3 SCCH - 7 unoffending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-J-8696 along with his wife Smt. Sandya and her daughter Sathvik as pillion riders, at that time the driver/accused drove the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-NB-7687 in a rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle as a result the Petitioner and pillion riders were fell on the road and the pillion riders were sustained simple injuries and the rider / Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to ESI Hospital Peenya and thereafter for higher treatment he was shifted to Kanva Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as inpatient and undergone surgery therein and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenditure and other incidental charges.
In this regard the Complainant/Sandya has lodged complaint before the Yeshwanthapura Traffic police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.196/2023 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279, 337 & 338 of IPC and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
M.V.C.No.4086/2023 4 SCCH - 7 3. Further it is contended that, prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and he was aged about 25 years and he was doing Cement work and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m.

Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he lost his income and future prospective life,
happiness, and earning capacity and become disabled and dependent.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-04- NB-7687.
Respondent No.1 is the RC owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.

In response to the notice, the Respondent No.2 remained absent and placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement.

5. In the written statement of respondent No.1, he has admitted that he is the RC owner of the offending vehicle and denied the petition averments in part including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle and M.V.C.No.4086/2023 5 SCCH - 7 contended that the alleged accident occurred due to sole negligence and fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further it is contended that the driver of the offending car was possessing valid and effective driving licence and the offending vehicle was duly insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance company and any liability, i.e., fastened on him would have to be indemnify by the Respondent No.2 and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.
:: I S S U E S ::
(1) Whether the Petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-NB-7687 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
(4) What order or award?

The Respondent No.1 got examined himself as RW-1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5 and closed their side.
8. Heard the arguments of both side.

10. Issue No.1:- This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act  1989 for seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the alleged accident.

11. The petitioner in the petition has contended that, on 08.05.2023 at about 5-40 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Yeshwanthapura Traffic Police Station, in front of Shakthi Health Meats Pvt. Ltd.,
near Surana college, ESI M.V.C.No.4086/2023 7 SCCH - 7 Hospital road, when the Petitioner was riding the unoffending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-J-8696 along with his wife Smt. Sandya and her daughter Sathvik as pillion riders, at that time the driver/accused drove the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-NB-7687 in a rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle as a result the Petitioner and pillion riders were fell on the road and the pillion riders were sustained simple injuries and the rider / Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to ESI Hospital Peenya and thereafter for higher treatment he was shifted to Kanva Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as inpatient and undergone surgery therein.
It is contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Respondent No.1 has admitted that he is the RC owner of the offending vehicle and denied the petition averments in part including age,
avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the alleged accident occurred due to sole negligence and fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further it is contended that the M.V.C.No.4086/2023 8 SCCH - 7 driver of the offending car was possessing valid and effective driving licence and the offending vehicle was duly insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance company and any liability, i.e., fastened on him would have to be indemnify by the Respondent No.2 and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
12.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.

Hence, in order to prove his case,
the Petitioner himself examined as P.W.1 and he has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.15 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.

In support of the Petitioner's case and in order to substantiate the oral evidence of P.W.1, the Petitioner has examined another two witnesses by name Nishith, as Pw.2, by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N., as PW.3.
I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.

Ex.P-1 is the True copy of FIR, Ex.P-2 is the True copy of complaint, Ex.P-2 (a) is the Statement of injured, Ex.P-3 is the true copy of the spot Panchanama, Ex.P.4 is the true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P-5 is the IMV report, Ex.P-6 is the true copy of Wound Certificate, Ex.P-7 is the true copy of Charge M.V.C.No.4086/2023 9 SCCH - 7 Sheet, Ex.P8 is the Sec.133 notice, Ex.P9 is the Reply to notice, Ex.P.10 is the Police Intimation, Ex.P-11 is the Discharge Summary, Ex.P-12 is the Hospital and Medical bills, Ex.P-13 is the Medical Prescriptions, Ex.P- 14 is the X-ray Film and Sachin vs Abhishek Bhattacherjee on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59830641/
4 Ex.P-15 is the Adhar Card.

13. In the examination in chief of PW.2 he has deposed that he is working as MRD of Kanva Sri Sai Hospital and he has produced Ex.P-16/Authorization letter, Ex.P-17/IP Record, Ex.P-18/ MLC Record, Ex.P-19/Police Intimation and Ex.P-20/X-ray Film.
14.

In order to prove the version of respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 got examined himself as R.W.1 and he has reiterated the entire version averments and contentions taken in the course of written statement in his evidence before this Court and also he has produced as many as Ex.R.1 to Ex.P-5 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the RW-1.

Ex.R.1 is the driving licence of wife of Respondent No.1,
Ex.R.2 is the Registration certificate of vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-NB-7687, Ex.R.3 is the insurance policy of TATA Altroz vehicle with Respondent No.2 Insurance Company, Ex.R.4 is the Online copy of insurance policy of TATA Altroz vehicle with Respondent No.2 Insurance M.V.C.No.4086/2023 10 SCCH - 7 Company /Zuno General Insurance Ltd., and Ex.R.5 is the Certificate issued under Section 65B of Evidence Act.

In the cross-examination of RW-1 by the counsels for Petitioner he has deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle is his wife and she was driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident and he was inmate of the offending vehicle.

The police have filed Charge Sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and the driver pleaded guilty before the court and paid the fine amount in relating to alleged accident case and he has not challenged the Charge Sheet.
Further he has denied that the alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the driver of the offending vehicle and no fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle.
Further he had denied that in order to escape from the liability he has filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.

15. On careful reading of Ex.P5/Motor Vehicle Accident Inspection Report it specifies that the Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said incident did not occur because of the mechanical defects in respect of the said offending vehicle.

Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the offending vehicle and opined that, left hand side front bumper broken, left M.V.C.No.4086/2023 11 SCCH - 7 hand side head light assembly broken and left hand side bonnet dent and scratched.

Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the unoffending vehicle and opined that, front mudguard broken, head light assembly broken, front and rear side all indicators are broken, handle damaged, crash guard scratched, both sides body cover broken, silencer scratched and right hand side foot rest damaged.
16.

On going through the Ex.P-6/Wound Certificate it is seen that the Doctor opined that the Petitioner was treated at Kanva Health Care Pvt. Ltd., and in the said alleged accident the Petitioner has sustained 1. laceration over cheek, 2. Abrasion over forehead, 3. fracture of skull bone, 4.
Fracture of nasal bone and 5. Fracture of right fibula.
Further the doctor opined that the injury No. 1 and 2 are simple in nature and injury No.3 to 5 are grievous in nature.

17. On going through the Ex.P-2/Complaint it is seen that on 08.05.2023 at about 5-40 p.m., in front of Shakthi Health Meats Pvt. Ltd., near Surana college, ESI Hospital road, when the Petitioner was riding the unoffending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-J-8696 along with his wife Smt.

5 Sandya and her daughter Sathvik as pillion riders, at that time the driver/accused M.V.C.No.4086/2023 12 SCCH - 7 drove the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-NB-7687 in a rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle as a result the Petitioner and pillion riders were fell on the road and the pillion riders were sustained simple injuries and the rider / Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to ESI Hospital Peenya and thereafter for higher treatment he was shifted to Kanva Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as inpatient and undergone surgery therein.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
18. On going through the Ex.P3/spot Mahazar it is seen that in pursuance of the alleged Ex.P2/complaint, on 09.05.2023, informant/Sandya.R showed the place of incident to the police.

The police have conducted the detailed spot mahazar in the presence of panch witnesses and prepared Ex.P-4 spot Sketch.
19.
Admittedly, the accused is the driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that,
Petitioner sustained grievous injury due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

The counsel for Respondent No.1 claimed the said Accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.1 M.V.C.No.4086/2023 13 SCCH - 7 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle,
slowly she may be driving and therefore she cannot be held to be negligent and the alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle, hence there is no negligence in the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, mahazar, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in M.V.C.No.4086/2023 14 SCCH - 7 the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the unoffending vehicle, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Complaint,
Ex.P3/spot Mahazar, Ex.P-4/Spot Sketch, Ex.P-5/MVA report, Ex.P-6/Wound Certificate,
Ex.P-7/Charge Sheet, Ex.P-8/Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act and Ex.P-9/ reply to the Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P6/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the Sachin vs Abhishek Bhattacherjee on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59830641/
6 offending vehicle, it resulted in the M.V.C.No.4086/2023 15 SCCH - 7 injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as she/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

20. Issue No.2 and 3:- The Learned counsel for the Petitioner has contended that the injured Petitioner was aged about 25 years and he was doing Cement work and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.,
and the Petitioner has incurred heavy expenses towards medical expenditure.

As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses,
special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

21. On the other hand the learned counsel for Respondent No.1 contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that his earning was about Rs.25,000/- p.m., the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.
Since the Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards M.V.C.No.4086/2023 16 SCCH - 7 such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.

22. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 25 years and he relied on the Ex.P.15/Aadhar Card of the Petitioner, wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 26.09.1995 and this accident was took place on 08.05.2023.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 27 years 7 months.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 27 years.
23. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was doing Cement work and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
But he has not produced single piece of documents to prove his actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the Petitioner taken at Rs.15,250/-.

. In the chief examination of PW-3/Dr.Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bengaluru, deposed that in the alleged road traffic accident the petitioner has sustained head injury with multiple skull bone fracture, nasal bone fracture and right fibula fracture and the Petitioner was treated at Kanva Hospital and later the Petitioner got treated with an asteopath and the Petitioner now complains of pain and swelling of the right ankle, unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg and carry his work coolie.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further deposed that on examination the Petitioner has swollen right ankle, restricted right ankle movements and recent X-ray shows united fracture and the Petitioner has sustained physical disability of the right lower limb at 30% and whole body disability at 10%.
In support of his oral evidence, the doctor/PW-3 has produced Ex.P-21/X-ray Film and Ex.P-22/Clinical notes .

Sachin vs Abhishek Bhattacherjee on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59830641/
7 25.

As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as working as Cement work while doing his work the petitioner has to stand and sit for long time, he has to bend, put weight on both legs, he has to sit down while doing the work.
But due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident the petitioner has not in position to do M.V.C.No.4086/2023 18 SCCH - 7 work as past.
The doctor has assessed the physical disability of the right lower limb at 30% and whole body disability at 10%.
Hence by considering the age, occupation, nature of injury and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 10% to the whole body.
26. With regard to the quantum, the age of the petitioner is considered as 27 years and the income is considered at Rs.15,250/- p.m.
As per Sarala Varma's Case the multiplier 17 is applicable and functional disability is considered at 10%.

On considering the avocation and age of the petitioner,
the total loss of future income is calculated as (Rs.15,250/- X 12 X 17 X 10/100) = Rs.3,11,100/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs.3,11,100/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.

27. In the alleged accident the petitioner has sustained laceration over cheek, abrasion over forehead, fracture of skull bone, Fracture of nasal bone and fracture of right fibula which shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering, mental agony.

. Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital for a period from 08.05.2023 to 12.05.2023, i.e., for a period of 5 days.

Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.15,000/- (Rs.3,000/- per day X 5 days)
under head of special diet and conveyance.
29. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
30. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.91,500/- (Rs.15,250/- x 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
31. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical expenses as per Ex.P.12 for an amount of Rs.62,677/-.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.62,677/- under the head of hospital and medical expenses.

The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:

34.
Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 and 3 are partly in the affirmative.

: In the result I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,80,277/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Eighty Thousand Two Hundred and Seventy Seven only) with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Further, Respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

(1) Whether the Petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-NB-7687 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
(4) What order or award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Respondent No.1 has admitted that he is the RC owner of the offending vehicle and denied the petition averments in part including age,
avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the alleged accident occurred due to sole negligence and fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it is contended that the M.V.C.No.4086/2023 8 SCCH - 7 driver of the offending car was possessing valid and effective driving licence and the offending vehicle was duly insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance company and any liability, i.e., fastened on him would have to be indemnify by the Respondent No.2 and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
12.
The counsel for Respondent No.1 claimed the said Accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.1 M.V.C.No.4086/2023 13 SCCH - 7 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle,
slowly she may be driving and therefore she cannot be held to be negligent and the alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle, hence there is no negligence in the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses,
special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.
Since the Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards M.V.C.No.4086/2023 16 SCCH - 7 such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in M.V.C.No.4086/2023 14 SCCH - 7 the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the unoffending vehicle, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P6/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the Sachin vs Abhishek Bhattacherjee on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59830641/
6 offending vehicle, it resulted in the M.V.C.No.4086/2023 15 SCCH - 7 injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as she/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
But he has not produced single piece of documents to prove his actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.
But due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident the petitioner has not in position to do M.V.C.No.4086/2023 18 SCCH - 7 work as past.
Hence by considering the age, occupation, nature of injury and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 10% to the whole body.

ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,80,277/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Eighty Thousand Two Hundred and Seventy Seven only) with interest @

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
